title.quote: G4SATBench: Benchmarking and Advancing SAT Solving with Graph Neural Networks
title.justification: Title as given on the first page.
title.value: G4SATBench: Benchmarking and Advancing SAT Solving with Graph Neural Networks

extractions.description: A benchmark study (G4SATBench) that curates 7 synthetic SAT datasets at 3 difficulty levels and evaluates a range of GNN-based SAT solvers (NeuroSAT, GCN, GGNN, GIN on LCG*/VCG*) across satisfiability prediction, satisfying assignment prediction, and unsat-core variable prediction, with supervised and unsupervised objectives and different inference algorithms; it further compares GNN solving behaviour with CDCL and local-search heuristics.

type.quote: we present G4SATBench, the first benchmark study that establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework for GNN-based SAT solvers
type.justification: The paper is an empirical benchmarking study with extensive experiments.

name.quote: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising approach for solving the Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT)
name.justification: The paper advances benchmarking of GNN-based SAT solving.
name.value: SAT solving with Graph Neural Networks

name.quote: the recent rapid advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) (Li et al., 2016; Kipf & Welling, 2017; Xu et al., 2019) have shown impressive performances in analyzing structured data
name.justification: Graph representation learning is the modelling framework used and evaluated.
name.value: Graph neural networks / graph representation learning

name.quote: The Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT) is a crucial problem at the nexus of computer science, logic, and operations research
name.justification: Combinatorial optimisation / logic is the application domain used as setting.

name.quote: we provide a diverse range of GNN models, including NeuroSAT (Selsam et al., 2019), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) (Kipf & Welling, 2017), Gated Graph Neural Network (GGNN) (Li et al., 2016), and Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) (Xu et al., 2019), on the both LCG* and VCG*.
name.justification: NeuroSAT is a re-implemented GNN baseline executed in all benchmarks.

is_contributed.quote: we re-implement various GNN-based SAT solvers with unified interfaces and configuration settings
is_contributed.justification: NeuroSAT is a prior model re-implemented, not contributed.

is_executed.quote: Each experiment is performed on a single RTX8000 GPU and 16 AMD EPYC 7502 CPU cores
is_executed.justification: NeuroSAT was trained and evaluated on GPUs.

is_compared.quote: Among all GNN models, the different graph constructions do not seem to have a significant impact on the results, and NeuroSAT (on LCG*) and GGNN (on VCG*) achieve the best overall performance.
is_compared.justification: Compared numerically with other GNN models.
